items.title: Empowering India's Digital Future through Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics
items.abstract: Abstract India’s digital transformation is creating a growing need for intelligent systems that can operate reliably across diverse sectors and linguistic settings. This paper presents a conceptual review of the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI), mathematics, and India’s digital development. The discussion focuses on agriculture, education, banking and financial services, legal services, transportation, digital commerce, and industry. Particular attention is given to the mathematical ideas that underpin AI: linear algebra for representing data and parameters; probability and statistics for uncertainty and inference; calculus for gradient-based learning; and optimization for selecting model parameters and making decisions. Mathematical modelling is further considered as a bridge between real-world systems and data-driven methods. The paper also examines responsible and inclusive AI, emphasizing reliability, privacy, fairness, transparency, security, accountability, and human oversight. India’s national AI strategy and the India’s AI Mission provide a policy context for these developments, while recent international assessment work highlights the importance of human-centred and ethical deployment. The paper argues that India’s long-term AI capacity should be developed through a coordinated emphasis on computing infrastructure, high-quality data, mathematical education, interdisciplinary research, multilingual technologies, and responsible governance.

items.title: Fault recognition approach applied to a rotating machine supported by hydrodynamic bearings using explainable artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract Rotating machines are widely employed in modern industry. The growing demand for efficiency and operational durability drives the development of intelligent rotors equipped with Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods that promote the extension of equipment lifespan through proactive maintenance actions and reducing costs associated with unscheduled downtime. Some common failures in rotating machines, such as unbalance, misalignment, and cracks, have similar symptoms, making it difficult to diagnose accurately. The absence of labeled historical data and explainable models that are understandable to end users also makes using AI difficult in the industry environment. This work presents a fault diagnosis technique based on vibration analysis and explainable AI models in this context. The proposed methodology achieved high diagnostic performance, with precision, recall, and F1-score exceeding 98.9% in numerical tests and demonstrating robust accuracy in experimental scenarios using a reduced set of 12 features. The methodology is demonstrated with interpretable applications that facilitate real-time fault diagnosis and proactive maintenance in rotating machinery, showcasing its potential for industrial implementation. Vibration responses are obtained through a representative finite element (FE) model of a horizontal rotor and its corresponding test rig. Techniques for feature extraction and selection are also employed. Ensemble clustering is performed for novelty detection, while traditional supervised approaches are used for classification purposes. The explainable AI tool is used to interpret the results, revealing that features such as the second harmonic of the rotational speed (A2X-S1) and skewness (R08-S1), both extracted from plane S1 in axial direction, play a critical role in distinguishing between similar fault patterns. The combination of robust performance and the possibility of interpretation from the output models demonstrates the potential of the proposed approach for fault recognition in rotating systems.

items.title: From Dependence To Independence: Work, Economy, And The Changing Future Of Work In English Literature With Special Reference To Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre, Elizabeth Gaskell's North And South And Virginia Woolf's A Room Of One's Own
items.abstract: Literature is a mirror of society. It shows the economic conditions, social problems, and daily struggles of human life across different times. Work is one of the most important parts of human life. In the past, many people depended completely on land, rich masters, or family heads for their survival. Over time, the meaning of work has changed from total dependence to economic independence. English literature presents many stories of characters who fight against poverty and social rules to earn their own living and live with dignity. Work is not just a way to earn money; it also gives a person self-respect, identity, and personal freedom. This research paper examines how work, economy, and independence are presented in selected English literary texts: Charlotte Brontë’s Jane Eyre, Elizabeth Gaskell’s North and South, and Virginia Woolf’s A Room of One’s Own. These texts show how education, employment, and money help individuals to become free and confident. Finally, this paper connects these literary lessons with the modern world. Today, technology, artificial intelligence, online platforms, and work-from-home jobs are changing the future of work. The paper concludes that even in the modern digital age, human dignity and economic security are essential for true freedom.

items.title: From Digital Infrastructure to Decision Intelligence: A Framework for Data-Driven Governance in Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a digital governance architecture that can transform rapidly expanding volumes of public data into timely, evidence-based, inclusive, transparent, and sustainable policy outcomes. This paper develops an integrated conceptual framework for data-driven digital governance by examining the complementary roles of Data Analytics, Business Intelligence (BI), Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI). Drawing on conceptual analysis and secondary evidence, the study conceptualizes DPI as the foundational layer for interoperable and trusted digital services, while Data Analytics and BI enable the transformation of data into descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive intelligence. Responsible AI further strengthens forecasting, simulation, decision support, and adaptive governance while incorporating principles of transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, security, and human oversight. A key contribution of the study is the proposed six-level BI maturity model, progressing from Digitization and Reporting to Diagnostic BI, Predictive Analytics, Decision Intelligence, and Adaptive Governance. The model addresses the challenge of dashboard-oriented governance by emphasising the progression from data availability to actionable intelligence, informed decision-making, outcome measurement, and continuous policy feedback. The study also identifies critical barriers, including data fragmentation, interoperability constraints, privacy and cybersecurity risks, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, institutional capability gaps, and inadequate outcome measurement. To address these challenges, a phased 2027–2047 strategic roadmap is proposed, beginning with common data standards and institutional analytics capacity and progressing toward interoperable, AI-assisted, outcome-oriented, and continuously learning governance systems. The paper argues that India’s long-term digital governance advantage will depend not merely on achieving digitalization at population scale, but on developing the institutional and technological capacity to convert data into intelligence, intelligence into informed decisions, and decisions into measurable and inclusive public value.

items.title: From Digital Infrastructure to Decision Intelligence: A Framework for Data-Driven Governance in Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a digital governance architecture that can transform rapidly expanding volumes of public data into timely, evidence-based, inclusive, transparent, and sustainable policy outcomes. This paper develops an integrated conceptual framework for data-driven digital governance by examining the complementary roles of Data Analytics, Business Intelligence (BI), Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI). Drawing on conceptual analysis and secondary evidence, the study conceptualizes DPI as the foundational layer for interoperable and trusted digital services, while Data Analytics and BI enable the transformation of data into descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive intelligence. Responsible AI further strengthens forecasting, simulation, decision support, and adaptive governance while incorporating principles of transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, security, and human oversight. A key contribution of the study is the proposed six-level BI maturity model, progressing from Digitization and Reporting to Diagnostic BI, Predictive Analytics, Decision Intelligence, and Adaptive Governance. The model addresses the challenge of dashboard-oriented governance by emphasising the progression from data availability to actionable intelligence, informed decision-making, outcome measurement, and continuous policy feedback. The study also identifies critical barriers, including data fragmentation, interoperability constraints, privacy and cybersecurity risks, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, institutional capability gaps, and inadequate outcome measurement. To address these challenges, a phased 2027–2047 strategic roadmap is proposed, beginning with common data standards and institutional analytics capacity and progressing toward interoperable, AI-assisted, outcome-oriented, and continuously learning governance systems. The paper argues that India’s long-term digital governance advantage will depend not merely on achieving digitalization at population scale, but on developing the institutional and technological capacity to convert data into intelligence, intelligence into informed decisions, and decisions into measurable and inclusive public value.

Libraries that were once physical repositories of printed material are now providing greater access to e-books, e-journals, digital repositories, online databases, and institutional resources. The next frontier in this evolution is the creation of intelligent knowledge hubs, enabled by new technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing, natural language processing, and multilingual systems. Intelligent libraries have the potential to be critical knowledge infrastructures for education, research, innovation, digital literacy, skill development, and lifelong learning in the context of Viksit Bharat @2047. Digital resources and remote information services can help bridge the knowledge divide between rural and urban communities, while multilingual digital content can enhance information access for a diverse range of users. At the same time, the development of intelligent knowledge hubs also presents a number of challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, skills gaps, data privacy, cybersecurity, copyright, and ethical issues around AI. Consequently, technological development needs to be supported by well-trained library professionals, robust security measures, ethical practices, and user-focused policies. By taking an inclusive and sustainable approach, intelligent libraries can play a significant role in advancing a knowledge-driven, digitally empowered, and inclusive Viksit Bharat @2047

items.title: From Ratings to Sensors: Real-Time AIIoT-Based Credibility Anchored on Blockchain for Ride-Sharing Ecosystems
items.abstract: Current ride-sharing platforms predominantly rely on subjective post-ride ratings to evaluate driver credibility, making reputation systems vulnerable to user bias, delayed feedback, collusion, and manipulation. Although recent studies have explored blockchain-based ride-sharing, AI-driven driver monitoring, and IoT-enabled transportation independently, they do not provide an integrated trust framework that continuously derives credibility from objectively verifiable driving behaviour while maintaining scalability and low operational cost.This paper presents Ridezy, a decentralized trust architecture that replaces conventional rating-based reputation with real-time sensor-driven credibility. The proposed framework combines edge Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (AIIoT) technologies to continuously monitor behavioural indicators such as lane discipline, speed compliance, braking behaviour, and traffic sign adherence. Instead of storing high-frequency telemetry on the blockchain, Ridezy employs a hybrid architecture in which behavioural summaries are processed off-chain and only cryptographic hashes, credibility updates, and payment records are anchored on Polygon smart contracts, enabling tamper-evident trust with minimal blockchain overhead. To evaluate the proposed architecture, Ridezy is compared against three representative trust models: a traditional rating-based system, an AI-only architecture, and a blockchain-only architecture. The evaluation considers behavioural detection performance, end-to-end latency, cost efficiency, throughput, reputation stability, tamper resistance, and component-wise ablation studies. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid architecture achieves higher behavioural fidelity and stronger trust guarantees than conventional reputation mechanisms while maintaining low per-ride blockchain cost and scalable operation through batched on-chain commitments.The primary contribution of this work is a sensor-driven credibility framework that transforms real-time behavioural evidence into a cryptographically verifiable trust primitive for ride-sharing ecosystems. By combining edge AI, IoT telemetry, and blockchain-based trust anchoring within a scalable hybrid architecture, Ridezy provides a practical foundation for trustworthy, transparent, and next-generation intelligent mobility systems.

items.title: GAN-Enhanced Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening: A Comprehensive Survey
items.abstract: Abstract Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by difficulties in social communication and interaction, together with restricted or repetitive patterns of behavior. Early screening is important for facilitating timely clinical assessment and intervention; however, conventional screening approaches often depend on clinical expertise, behavioral observation, developmental history, and standardized assessment tools. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have created new opportunities for data-driven and automated ASD screening. This survey provides a comprehensive review of AI-based approaches for ASD screening, with particular emphasis on multimodal learning and the integration of heterogeneous data sources. Behavioral, genetic, environmental, neuroimaging, physiological, and clinical data modalities are examined, along with approaches for combining information across multiple sources. The survey further reviews the role of GANs and related generative approaches in synthetic-data generation and data augmentation, particularly in addressing challenges associated with limited and imbalanced datasets. Multimodal fusion strategies, multi-input neural networks, and emerging deep learning approaches are also discussed in the context of ASD screening. The reviewed literature indicates that multimodal AI has the potential to provide a more comprehensive representation of ASD-related characteristics than single-modality approaches. However, important challenges remain, including limited and heterogeneous datasets, class imbalance, multimodal data integration, GAN training instability, synthetic-data quality, privacy and security, model interpretability, generalizability, and limited external clinical validation. This survey identifies these challenges and highlights research directions toward reliable, explainable, privacy-preserving, and clinically validated AI-based multimodal ASD screening systems. Keywords: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); Artificial Intelligence; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs); Multimodal Learning; ASD Screening; Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data

items.title: Generative AI-Assisted Competitive Microlearning Strategy: Development and Validation of the Plomp Model in Classroom Teacher Education in Finland
items.abstract: Background. The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has created challenges in designing responsible and adaptive learning strategies. Meanwhile, competitive elements in gamified learning remain debated due to inconsistent effects on learner engagement. Purpose. This research aimed to develop and evaluate a generative AI-assisted competitive microlearning strategy for improving instructional media development skills among Finnish Luokanopettajakoulutus (Class Teacher Education) students. Novelty. This study introduces a novel instructional design that integrates generative AI, microlearning, and optional quality-based competition. Unlike conventional competitive gamification approaches, the proposed strategy recognizes learner differences by examining whether competition produces varied outcomes across learning groups Method. Using the Plomp development model, the study involved 79 undergraduate students from four parallel classes. Data from expert validation, practicality questionnaires, and product assessments were analyzed using Aiken’s V and descriptive statistics. Results. The strategy achieved high validity (Aiken’s V = 0.87) and strong practicality (83.1% student response; 85.9% lecturer response). Variation in competition participation (41–62%) indicated different effects among learner groups. Conclusion. The findings contribute an adaptive AI-assisted microlearning framework that balances innovation, learner diversity, and educational equity in teacher education.

items.title: Grand Theft Autocomplete: 'AI' enclosures and their threat to data sovereignty
items.abstract: The way we distribute research data and software today relies heavily on the open web: largely standardised formats, decentralised data hubs, public availability, affordable compute, free learning resources, and findability afforded by a few ad-supported web indexes. This openness, however, is increasingly under threat. The companies that currently attempt to monetise large language models also make it much harder to keep websites online and position their chat interfaces as intermediaries between knowledge and users. The ‘AI’-enclosed web empowers Big Tech to further interfere in learning, education, and research. This talk draws a parallel to the historical appropriation of common land in 18th- and 19th-century England. With this historical revolution of the rich against the poor to learn from, it outlines the specific dangers to the knowledge commons in the next few years. In conclusion, the talk attempts to identify what can be done to preserve and and empower individual, institutional, and transnational data sovereignty in the face of this not entirely new threat: critique the neoreactionary ideology behind the technology, empower ‘boring’ technology, identify affordable machine-learning tech, and embrace local and peer-to-peer computing.

items.title: Grand Theft Autocomplete: 'AI' enclosures and their threat to data sovereignty
items.abstract: The way we distribute research data and software today relies heavily on the open web: largely standardised formats, decentralised data hubs, public availability, affordable compute, free learning resources, and findability afforded by a few ad-supported web indexes. This openness, however, is increasingly under threat. The companies that currently attempt to monetise large language models also make it much harder to keep websites online and position their chat interfaces as intermediaries between knowledge and users. The ‘AI’-enclosed web empowers Big Tech to further interfere in learning, education, and research. This talk draws a parallel to the historical appropriation of common land in 18th- and 19th-century England. With this historical revolution of the rich against the poor to learn from, it outlines the specific dangers to the knowledge commons in the next few years. In conclusion, the talk attempts to identify what can be done to preserve and and empower individual, institutional, and transnational data sovereignty in the face of this not entirely new threat: critique the neoreactionary ideology behind the technology, empower ‘boring’ technology, identify affordable machine-learning tech, and embrace local and peer-to-peer computing.

items.title: Human-Centered AI Education for Viksit Bharat @2047: Reimagining Teachers, Learners and Future-Ready Schools
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence is reshaping how societies function, communicate, learn and innovate, and India stands at a particularly consequential point in this shift. The arrival of generative AI, adaptive learning platforms and intelligent digital tools presents the country with both a rare opportunity and a demanding policy challenge on its path toward Viksit Bharat @2047. Education sits at the heart of this challenge, because the citizens, workers and innovators who will carry that vision forward are being shaped right now, inside today's classrooms. This conceptual paper asks how Artificial Intelligence can genuinely strengthen India's education system without eroding the human qualities that make learning meaningful: agency, creativity, ethics and social responsibility. Drawing on an integrative reading of policy documents and international literature - UNESCO's AI competency frameworks, OECD perspectives on AI literacy, India's National Education Policy 2020, the IndiaAI Mission, the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, ILO research on generative AI and employment, and the author's own practitioner book AI and Us - the paper argues that the real question is not whether AI will replace teachers, but whether schools can build a working partnership between teachers, learners and AI. The paper introduces a Human-Centered AI Education Framework built around six interlocking dimensions: AI Literacy, AI-Augmented Pedagogy, Human Skills, Ethical and Responsible Use, Inclusive Digital Infrastructure, and Continuous Professional Learning. It also sketches a Teacher-AI-Student ecosystem in which AI takes on assistive and analytical work while teachers hold on to pedagogical, relational and ethical authority. Viksit Bharat @2047, the paper contends, does not just need citizens who are skilled at using AI - it needs citizens who are AI-literate, critical, creative, ethical and socially engaged. The paper closes with policy recommendations aimed at schools, teacher-education institutions, government bodies and educational technology developers.

items.title: Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Digital Governance in India: A Review of Digital Public Services.
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to improve public service delivery through automation, data analysis, decision support and digital interaction. In India, Digital India, Digital Public Infrastructure and national AI initiatives have created opportunities to make government services more efficient, accessible and responsive. At the same time, AI-enabled public services raise concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accessibility, accountability and citizen trust. This paper examines how a Human-Centred AI (HCAI) approach can support sustainable digital governance in India through a structured review of secondary literature. Recent peer-reviewed studies, government reports and institutional publications are examined using thematic analysis. The review focuses on citizen-centric service delivery, accessibility and inclusion, transparency and explainability, privacy and security, fairness, citizen trust, and human oversight. The findings indicate that AI can support intelligent service discovery, conversational assistance, multilingual interaction, personalisation and routine administrative processing. However, technological capability alone does not guarantee better public services. AI must be designed around citizen needs and supported by appropriate governance safeguards. Based on the synthesis, the paper proposes a conceptual Human-Centred AI Framework with five interconnected dimensions: human needs, inclusive digital experience, responsible AI, accountable governance and sustainable public value. The paper concludes that India's AI-enabled digital governance should balance technological innovation with accessibility, privacy, fairness, transparency, human oversight and public trust.

items.title: Hyper-Personalization vs. Privacy Paradox: Balancing AI-Driven Customer Insights with Consumer Data Ethics and Trust
items.abstract: Abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence and machine learning has enabled organizations to achieve unprecedented levels of hyper-personalization, transforming how brands interact with consumers. However, this capability intensifies the privacy paradox, a phenomenon where consumers express profound concern for data privacy while simultaneously trading personal information for tailored experiences and immediate utility. This paper examines the complex equilibrium required to harness AI-driven customer insights without eroding consumer data ethics and organizational trust. Traditional data collection frameworks are increasingly inadequate in managing the granular, predictive datasets utilized by modern personalization algorithms. As predictive analytics decipher behavioral patterns, purchasing intent, and real-time location data, the ethical threshold for consent, transparency, and data minimization rises significantly. Organizations frequently struggle to balance the commercial imperatives of hyper-targeted engagement with regulatory compliance, such as the General Data Protection Regulation and evolving global privacy standards. This research investigates how opaque data practices and aggressive profiling lead to algorithmic fatigue, consumer alienation, and catastrophic trust erosion. The study analyzes the mechanics of transparent data stewardship, exploring how organizations can implement ethical AI frameworks that prioritize consumer agency, explicit consent architecture, and explainable algorithmic models. By adopting privacy-by-design principles and federated learning techniques, businesses can derive deep consumer insights without compromising individual anonymity or data security. Furthermore, the paper highlights the strategic advantage of ethical positioning, demonstrating that transparent data practices transform compliance from a legal burden into a distinct market differentiator. Methodologically, this study combines a comprehensive review of contemporary digital ethics literature with empirical case analyses of firms navigating data breaches versus those successfully cultivating trust-based personalization ecosystems. The findings reveal that sustainable customer lifetime value is directly correlated with perceived data fairness and control. Ultimately, the paper provides a strategic roadmap for leaders to align AI-driven marketing capabilities with robust ethical safeguards, ensuring that hyper-personalization fosters long-term brand loyalty rather than opportunistic exploitation.

items.title: Impact of AI-Enabled Features in Faculty Teaching Effectiveness in Google Classroom
items.abstract: Abstract The Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into education is transforming traditional teaching and learning practices. Google Classroom, currently with AI-enabled features such as lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, rubric development, differentiated learning resources, and suggested feedback, provides faculty with special power to improve teaching efficiency and classroom management. This study examines the impact of AI-enabled features on faculty teaching effectiveness in Google Classroom. The study mainly focuses on how AI influences lesson planning, preparation time, assessment, feedback, personalization of learning, student engagement, and overall teaching effectiveness. The study can be conducted using a structured questionnaire among faculty members who use Google Classroom. The findings are expected to show that AI can reduce routine workload and support more efficient and personalized teaching. However, factors such as AI literacy, training, accuracy of AI-generated content, privacy concerns, and the need for human supervision may influence its effectiveness. Research on AI in education also emphasizes the importance of teacher professional development and responsible implementation.

items.title: Impact of Generative AI on Formal Writing Skills of Undergraduate students
items.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has significantly influenced students' approach to formal writing. The present research, titled “Impact of Generative AI on the Formal Writing Practices of Undergraduate Students,” tries to examine the extent, frequency, purposes, and perceived effects of Generative AI used by undergraduate students in formal writing. A descriptive survey research design along with a quantitative approach was applied. A structured online questionnaire was prepared using Google Forms to collect primary data from undergraduate students representing programmes such as B.A., BMS, BAF, B.Com., B.Sc. Computer Science, B.Sc. IT, Psychology, History, and B.A.M.M.C. A total of 108 responses were obtained. Non-probability convenience sampling was used, and responses were analysed on the basis of frequency and percentage analysis, along with interpretation of Likert-scale responses. The findings show that a considerable number of undergraduate students use Generative AI in formal writing practices, which is clear as 94 out of 108 respondents (86.9%) selecting previous use of Generative AI for formal writing. ChatGPT proved to be the most popular Generative AI tool used by the students, followed by Google Gemini and Claude. The study reveals students’ use of AI for generating ideas, drafting content, improving grammar and language, summarising information, and editing written work. This study is aimed at finding out the degree of AI help in formal writing, the level of students' improvement in their writing skills, confidence in writing without AI help, acceptance of AI-written content without major editing, and their readiness to keep using the tools. This study reveals the significance of Generative AI in the field of formal writing of undergraduates and the advantages, as well as possible drawbacks, connected to their dependence on the technology. These results can be helpful in studying the influence of Generative AI on the writing process of students and will help the educational institutions and teachers to encourage proper and ethical use of Generative AI by students.

items.abstract: Abstract: Science has emerged as one of the most influential forces shaping economic growth, social transformation and national progress in the twenty-first century. The development of modern societies is increasingly dependent on the ability to create scientific knowledge, translate that knowledge into technological innovations and ensure that these innovations reach different sections of society. For a country such as India, which is simultaneously addressing issues of economic development, population growth, employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy security and environmental sustainability, science has a particularly important role to play. Scientific advancement can provide evidence-based and innovative solutions to complex national challenges while also strengthening India's competitiveness in the global knowledge economy. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and First-Principles Physics for the Discovery of Sustainable Topological Heusler Materials: Prospects for Spintronics and Energy-Efficient Technologies in Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), first-principles computational methods, and advanced functional materials provides new opportunities for the accelerated discovery of energy-efficient quantum and spintronic materials. Heusler alloys are particularly attractive because their chemical composition and structural ordering can be systematically modified to obtain desirable magnetic, electronic, topological, and thermoelectric properties. Magnetic Heusler compounds with strong spin–orbit coupling can exhibit Weyl points, band crossings, Berry-curvature hotspots, and enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC). Representative literature systems demonstrate the potential of this materials family: Co2MnGa has a reported calculated AHC of approximately −1310 Scm⁻¹, while Co2MnAl reaches approximately −1631 Scm⁻¹; Co2CrAl illustrates strong Fermi-level dependence, with its AHC increasing from approximately −313 Scm⁻¹ to about 1089 Scm⁻¹ after energy tuning. This work proposes an integrated density functional theory (DFT) and AI framework for the systematic discovery and optimization of sustainable topological Heusler materials. DFT calculations provide the physics-based evaluation of structural stability, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, spin–orbit coupling, Berry curvature, AHC, and ANC, while machine-learning models can learn composition–structure–property relationships and accelerate screening across unexplored chemical spaces. The proposed workflow includes stability screening, magnetic-ground-state analysis, electronic and topological characterization, Berry-curvature calculations, anomalous transverse transport calculations, machine-learning prediction, and independent DFT validation. Chemical substitution and carrier tuning are considered as strategies for positioning topological features near the Fermi level and enhancing transverse transport. Literature examples such as Pt2CrRh, with reported AHC of approximately 1966 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 7.50 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, and (Co0. 8Ni0.2)2FeSn, with reported AHC of approximately −2568 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 8.27 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, illustrate the potential of chemical tuning for achieving large transverse responses. The proposed DFT–AI strategy can therefore provide an efficient route toward identifying promising materials for spintronics, spin-caloritronics, low-power electronics, and thermal-energy conversion.

items.title: Introducing the LISA Framework: Level and Integration Scope of Artificial Intelligence in Learning Design (Presentation at ICL 2026, Cologne, 09/2026)
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming learning design, yet current terminology often lacks the precision to distinguish between varying levels of AI involvement. Terms like "AI-supported" obscure critical differences in decision-making authority and adaptation dynamism. This presentation introduces the LISA Framework (Level of autonomy and Interaction Scope of AI in learning design), developed within the Erasmus+ project DigiSET. LISA proposes a two-dimensional typology based on (1) the Level of AI Autonomy (human-led assistance to fully autonomous operation) and (2) the Interaction Scope (static, rule-based execution vs. dynamic, comprehensive adaptation). Six archetypes emerge: the Content Generator, the Co-Creator, the Rule-Based Agent, the Smart Assistant, the Adaptive Partner, and the Autonomous Agent. Grounded in practical experiences from Graz University of Technology, this heuristic model provides educators, researchers, and policymakers with a structured vocabulary to analyze, discuss, and strategically plan AI-enhanced learning resources. This paper was presented by Benedikt Brünner. Citation: Schön, S., Brünner, B.& Ebner, M. (2026, September 30). items.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach
items.abstract: Abstract Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure–activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layer to capture the sequential nature of these patterns. This architecture also exploits an attention mechanism that computes attention weights across the sequence, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant molecular substructures for toxicity prediction. Toxic and nontoxic chemicals, represented by canonical SMILES, are investigated as the words of two languages which have to be discriminated; using eight different end points, the model provided an accurate description of toxicity patterns, with an average Area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.83 (min: 0.70, max: 0.94) under repeated cross-validation. The models were trained on relatively small data sets (∼1000 samples) and often strongly imbalanced, two important challenges that highlight the opportunities for future improvement; moreover, the proposed attention-based framework offers a representation of the molecular regions influencing model predictions, providing a basis for future investigations into toxicity-related structural patterns and potentially supporting hypothesis generation in drug design or drug repurposing applications.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development of Azo Dye-Based Metal Complexes with Antimicrobial Properties
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for accelerating scientific research, particularly in materials science, medicinal chemistry, coordination chemistry, and sustainable chemical development. Azo dye-based metal complexes represent an important class of coordination compounds because of their diverse structural characteristics, tunable electronic properties, and potential biological activities. However, conventional synthesis and screening of such complexes can be time-consuming, resource-intensive, and dependent on extensive experimental trials. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning can provide an efficient approach for predicting molecular properties, optimizing synthesis conditions, and identifying compounds with enhanced antimicrobial potential. The present study proposes an AI-assisted framework for the sustainable development of azo dye-based metal complexes with antimicrobial properties. In this approach, molecular descriptors, structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, metal-ion characteristics, and experimentally determined antimicrobial data can be integrated into machine-learning models. These models can be trained to establish structure–activity relationships and predict the antimicrobial performance of newly designed complexes before their experimental synthesis. Such predictive modelling may help researchers prioritize promising compounds and reduce unnecessary laboratory experimentation. The proposed approach also supports the principles of green and sustainable chemistry by potentially reducing chemical consumption, solvent use, energy requirements, experimental repetitions, and laboratory waste. AI can further assist in optimizing reaction parameters such as temperature, reaction time, solvent, pH, reactant ratio, and catalyst concentration to improve yield and efficiency. The integration of AI with coordination chemistry can therefore contribute to the development of safer, more efficient, and environmentally responsible antimicrobial materials. The approach is particularly relevant to India's emerging digital scientific ecosystem, where AI-enabled research can support innovation, reduce research costs, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, computational science, biotechnology, and data science. The study concludes that AI should be viewed as a complementary tool to experimental chemistry rather than a replacement for laboratory validation. Combining computational prediction with synthesis, characterization, and antimicrobial evaluation can provide a powerful pathway for developing novel azo dye-based metal complexes while supporting sustainable scientific development.

items.title: Making India a Knowledge Society in the Age of AI - Building India's Cognitive Infrastructure for Vikasit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper draws attention to the urgent need of building Cognitive Infrastructure along with the physical infrastructure for rapid development of the country. India is rapidly transitioning from developing economy to a developed economy unleashing many forces of rapid development and growth. The quest for Vikasit Bharat @2047 (India as a developed country) requires building the foundational cognitive-intellectual infrastructure and not just physical infrastructure. The development of the human capital with higher cognitive abilities capable to create, add and transact value through knowledge creation and utilisation. Continual innovation is critical for sustainable growth and development. Innovation is a direct outcome of the quality of the cognitive infrastructure. Nations compete on the strength of their cognitive infrastructure and not just on the availability of natural resources. Cognitive infrastructure is the most critical factor of production. To build a high-quality competitive cognitive infrastructure we need new ways of acquiring and utilising knowledge. Without cognitive abilities people cannot become knowledge workers to lead the cognitive shift happening all over the world in this age of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The race is now cognitive in nature and those nations with robust cognitive and physical infrastructure will be the leaders. India has to focus on developing the cognitive capital of the aspiring youth equipping the with cognitive abilities to respond to what is coming. The uncertainties caused by technological disruptions and geopolitical shifts are overwhelming. True security comes from building an ever-expanding and renewed cognitive infrastructure which is free from the laws of diminishing returns. This paper explores the need to take a fresh perspective of the emerging realities such as the shift from computing to cognitive, and recommends building futuristic cognitive infrastructure along with the physical infrastructure for realising the goal of Vikasit Bharat @2047. One core concern highlighted is the linguistic development as human development is fundamentally the cultivation of cognitive capacity—and language is one of the most powerful instruments for that cultivation.

items.title: NEP 2020, Digital Transformation and Skill-Based Education: A Roadmap for Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to emerge as a developed, inclusive, innovative, technologically advanced and knowledge-driven nation by the centenary of its independence. The achievement of this vision depends substantially on the quality of human capital developed through education. School education, in particular, has a foundational role because the students educated today will become the professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers, teachers, administrators, innovators and responsible citizens who will shape India's social and economic development in the coming decades. items.title: Post-Human Canvas: Literature As a Moral Compass for AI Integration and National Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence and smart technologies are rapidly evolving, opening up new opportunities for economic progress, but also raising complex ethical questions. Technological paradigms concentrate on efficiency, optimization, and material progress, but often lack the inherent frameworks to deal with existential, moral, and socio-cultural consequences. In this paper, it is argued that literature is an indispensable moral compass for ethical integration of AI, more so in the setting of national growth and sustainable development (like India’s Viksit Bharat vision). This study draws on contemporary post-human literature, eco-critical texts, and speculative narratives to argue that literary humanities provide algorithmic development critical empathy, ethical foresight, and socio-cultural grounding. This paper employs a qualitative, interdisciplinary methodology drawing on Post-Humanist Theory, Narrative Ethics and Hermeneutics to explore how literary tropes challenge technological determinism and articulate human-centric technological futures. The results show that it is impossible to achieve long-term national development based only on scientific innovation, and that a synergistic relationship between technical ability and humanistic ethics is necessary. This paper thus presents practical recommendations for the incorporation of literary studies into STEM curricula, AI ethics policy, and multidisciplinary research frameworks, to ensure that national technological progress is ethically grounded, socially inclusive, and humanely sustainable.

items.title: Renewable Energy Innovation: Emerging Technologies, Challenges, Opportunities and Its Role in Sustainable Development
items.abstract: Abstract Renewable energy innovation has become a critical component of the global transition toward a sustainable, secure, and low-carbon energy system. Growing energy demand, climate change, depletion of conventional fossil-fuel resources, and concerns regarding energy security have accelerated the development and adoption of renewable energy technologies. Innovation in solar photovoltaic systems, wind energy, hydropower, bioenergy, geothermal energy, green hydrogen, energy storage, smart grids, and digital energy-management systems is transforming the structure of modern energy systems. This research paper examines the concept, evolution, major technological developments, economic significance, environmental benefits, challenges, and future prospects of renewable energy innovation. It also discusses the role of artificial intelligence, Internet of Things technologies, advanced batteries, floating solar, offshore wind, green hydrogen, and decentralized energy systems in improving the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy. Particular attention is given to the Indian context, including India's renewable-energy potential, policy initiatives, technological development, and opportunities for sustainable economic growth. The paper adopts a descriptive and analytical research approach based primarily on secondary information from academic literature, institutional reports, government publications, and international energy organizations. The study finds that renewable energy innovation can reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, improve energy security, create employment, encourage technological development, and support inclusive economic growth. However, challenges such as intermittency, energy storage, high initial investment, grid integration, land requirements, financing constraints, supply-chain dependencies, and skill shortages must be addressed. The paper concludes that sustained investment in research and development, supportive public policy, private-sector participation, technological collaboration, and development of skilled human resources are essential for accelerating renewable energy innovation and achieving long-term sustainable development.

items.title: Representation of Artificial Intelligence in Contemporary Fiction
items.abstract: Abstract: The present research paper deals with the representation of artificial intelligence in the contemporary fiction. The rapid developments of artificial intelligence had generated corresponding proliferation of literary narratives concerned with intelligent machines, artificial consciousness, automation, human-machine intimacy and the boundaries of human world. While earlier science fiction often imagined intelligent machines primarily as either servants or threats; recent literature presents artificial intelligence in more complex roles such as companion, worker, friend, moral agent and political subject. Such representations make the distinction between human and machines very complex and redefine the concepts like consciousness, emotion, autonomy and responsibility. Hence, in this paper an attempt is made to take the review of AI reflected in the contemporary fiction. Keywords: artificial intelligence, contemporary fiction, science fiction, human-machine relationships, technology identity.

items.title: Rethinking Student Assignments in Higher Education in the Age of Generative AI: From Product Assessment to Process-Oriented Learning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can contribute to idea generation, content organisation, language editing, and product revision, making it difficult for teachers to judge students’ knowledge and understanding, cognitive engagement, and independent contribution solely from the final assignment. This study employed a focused integrative literature review and conducted structured extraction, source-type appraisal, thematic coding, and cross-text comparison across 37 materials: 24 GenAI-related studies, eight classic works on assessment theory, and five policy and guidance documents. The findings indicate that final products remain valuable for assessing students’ overall performance, but their explanatory power as a single source of learning evidence has diminished under conditions of human-AI co-production. Drawing on the literature synthesis, this article proposes a six-stage process-oriented assignment framework comprising task interpretation, independent attempt, human-AI interaction, information verification, outcome revision, and reflective disclosure. The framework is guided by alignment with learning outcomes, student agency, visibility of cognitive engagement, transparency and responsibility, and proportionality. It links sustainable assessment with long-term evaluative capability, responsible AI use, equitable participation, and manageable evidence requirements. As a literature-informed conceptual proposal, its effectiveness, scope of application, and implementation burden require examination across disciplines and course contexts.

items.title: Rethinking Student Assignments in Higher Education in the Age of Generative AI: From Product Assessment to Process-Oriented Learning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can contribute to idea generation, content organisation, language editing, and product revision, making it difficult for teachers to judge students’ knowledge and understanding, cognitive engagement, and independent contribution solely from the final assignment. This study employed a focused integrative literature review and conducted structured extraction, source-type appraisal, thematic coding, and cross-text comparison across 37 materials: 24 GenAI-related studies, eight classic works on assessment theory, and five policy and guidance documents. The findings indicate that final products remain valuable for assessing students’ overall performance, but their explanatory power as a single source of learning evidence has diminished under conditions of human-AI co-production. Drawing on the literature synthesis, this article proposes a six-stage process-oriented assignment framework comprising task interpretation, independent attempt, human-AI interaction, information verification, outcome revision, and reflective disclosure. The framework is guided by alignment with learning outcomes, student agency, visibility of cognitive engagement, transparency and responsibility, and proportionality. It links sustainable assessment with long-term evaluative capability, responsible AI use, equitable participation, and manageable evidence requirements. As a literature-informed conceptual proposal, its effectiveness, scope of application, and implementation burden require examination across disciplines and course contexts.

items.title: Sustainable Futures and Literary Voices: Eco-Criticism in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Abstract: The accelerating climate crisis and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a new intellectual landscape in which environmental sustainability no longer be discussed independently of technological development. Literature, as a cultural form capable of representing ecological relationships, technological anxieties, and alternative futures, has an important role in this debate. This paper examines how contemporary ecocriticism respond to the environmental challenges associated with artificial intelligence while also exploring the potential of AI to support environmental knowledge, literary interpretation, and sustainable futures. Drawing upon ecocritical theory, environmental humanities, posthumanism, Indigenous ecological thought, and recent scholarship on AI and environmental sustainability, the study analyses selected works including Margaret Atwood’s Oryx and Crake, Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement, Richard Powers’s The Overstory, Robin Wall Kimmerer’s Braiding Sweetgrass, and Donna J. Haraway’s Staying with the Trouble. The paper argues that these texts challenge anthropocentric assumptions by foregrounding interdependence among humans, nonhuman organisms, technologies, and ecological systems. Atwood exposes the destructive consequences of technological mastery; Ghosh identifies the limitations of literary forms that marginalize ecological catastrophe; Powers expands narrative attention from individual human lives to forests and multispecies networks; Kimmerer proposes reciprocity rather than domination as the basis of ecological ethics; and Haraway advocates “making-with” other species rather than seeking technological mastery over nature.

items.title: The AI Lexicon: Exploring Neologism and Contemporary Word Formation Processes
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence has rapidly become part of everyday communication, writing, education, media, and digital culture. While language has been traditionally understood as a human-created and his lexicon continuously evolving system, the emergence of generative AI raises a new question: Can machines become participants in language change? This paper examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and the formation of new words, expressions, and meanings. It focuses particularly on neologisms and word-formation processes, including Conversion, blending, compounding, clipping, acronym, affixation, and reduplication. The study argues that AI may not independently “own” or control language change, but it can increasingly act as a catalyst, amplifier, and collaborator in the evolution of vocabulary.

items.title: The Giving Of Reasons: Judgement Writing, Judicial Reasoning, and GenAI
items.abstract: This article focuses on the core judicial role of giving reasons for a judge’s decision and the use of generative artificial intelligence (‘GenAI’) tools based on LLMs in the crafting of judgments. Considering specifically GenAI and judgment writing in common law systems, it deals with the connection between the act of decision-making and the giving of reasons for that decision. Our argument is that judgment writing should remain the domain of human judges, for reasons that are both institutional (the impact on the judicial system) and individual or processual (the impact on judges performing their roles). We seek to analyse the nature and extent of judicial use of GenAI tools that preserves this as a human domain. Ultimately, we conclude that it is not appropriate to use GenAI for judgment writing, but peripheral or adjacent uses may be supportable, provided they do not undercut the core judicial role.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Different Aspects of the Society
items.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

items.title: The Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework: AI-Augmented Library Services for Inclusive Digital Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Innovation towards Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract India’s Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a knowledge-driven digital economy powered by artificial intelligence, inclusive entrepreneurship, FinTech, e-commerce and sustainable practices. Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions remain under-utilised as active intermediaries between knowledge resources and the competencies demanded by the future of work. This paper coins the Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework—an original, multi-layered LIS model that positions academic and public libraries as AI-enabled hubs for digital-commerce literacy, ethical information services and sustainable innovation. The study adopts a conceptual-constructive design that synthesises LIS theory, digital-economy literature, AI-ethics guidelines and national policy documents (NEP-2020, Digital India, Startup India). The KCB Framework comprises four interdependent layers: (1) Infrastructure and Multilingual Access, (2) AI Knowledge Processing, (3) User-Centric Commerce Services and (4) Ethical-Sustainable Governance. Expected outcomes include reduced information asymmetry for gig workers and micro-entrepreneurs, strengthened academia–industry–startup linkages, and measurable contributions to inclusive growth and the Sustainable Development Goals. The framework is offered as a replicable, emulable blueprint that other institutions can adapt, pilot and scale, thereby leaving a durable mark on both scholarship and practice.

items.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Qur'anic Education and Interpretation: A Phenomenological Study of Its Requirements among Scholars in Fars Province, Iran
items.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the requirements for employing artificial intelligence (AI) in Qur'anic education and interpretation, focusing on how Qur'anic scholars and instructors in Fars Province, Iran, perceive the conditions necessary for its effective, ethical, and pedagogically appropriate use. Design/methodology/approach - The study adopts a qualitative phenomenological design using Colaizzi's seven-step analytical procedure. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with ten faculty members in Qur'anic sciences and Hadith and experienced Qur'anic instructors in Fars Province. Participants were selected through purposive and theoretical sampling until theoretical saturation was achieved. The interview data were subjected to thematic analysis, with credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability addressed through validation procedures. Findings - The analysis generated three principal categories: preliminary and infrastructural requirements, foundational and principled requirements, and technical and operational requirements. These comprised eight subcategories and 45 sub-concepts. The findings indicate that AI can support personalized learning, Qur'anic recitation, comprehension, multimodal instruction, and the integration of Qur'anic knowledge. However, its effective use requires reliable infrastructure, organized and credible Qur'anic data, trained educators, ethical safeguards, source verification, content validation, professional supervision, and interdisciplinary cooperation. Research implications/limitations - The framework provides practical guidance for educational institutions, Qur'anic centers, policymakers, and technology developers. However, the study is limited by its ten participants from a single province and its reliance on self-reported perceptions rather than observed AI-supported instruction. Originality/value - The study provides an empirically grounded phenomenological framework that connects AI, Qur'anic pedagogy, and ethical requirements for sacred-text education, extending AI-in-education research into the specific epistemic context of Qur'anic learning and interpretation.

items.title: The trials methodology research agenda—an international multi-stakeholder priority setting exercise
items.abstract: Abstract Background Trials methodology research priorities must be regularly reassessed to address contemporary methodological challenges. Over a decade has passed since the original priority setting exercise surveyed UK clinical trials unit directors. We conducted a two-stage international, multi-stakeholder survey to identify and rank current priorities in clinical trial methodology. Methods Stakeholders—researchers, trialists, healthcare professionals, patient and public representatives, funders, research ethics committee members, and others—were recruited through professional networks and snowball sampling. In stage 1, participants responded to four open-ended questions covering trial planning, conduct, analysis, and reporting. Responses were categorised into 34 research questions. In stage 2, participants reviewed the questions in random order, selected their top 10, and ranked them. Reverse scoring was applied, with scores summed within stakeholder groups, converted to rank-based scores, and combined so each group contributed equally regardless of size. Additional questions were independently coded by two authors against the 34 predefined questions, and new themes identified. Results In stage 1, 274 participants from 20 countries provided 2409 suggestions, categorised under 34 research questions. In stage 2, 431 respondents from 25 countries participated, of whom 341 (79%) across seven stakeholder groups completed priority ranking. The top 10 priority questions (including a joint seventh rank) were (1) designing relevant and impactful trials, (2) ensuring representative participants, (3) improving recruitment, (4) identifying and prioritising outcomes, (5) using healthcare systems data, (6) participant involvement in planning, (7=) transparency of trials, (7=) optimising trial approvals, (9) reporting and presenting findings, and (10) sharing and communicating findings. The top three questions appeared in all seven stakeholder groups’ top 10. Patient and public representatives ( n = 40) ranked ‘participant involvement in planning’ highest, while ethics committee members ( n = 9) uniquely prioritised ‘consent and safety’. ‘Innovative trials designs’ and ‘artificial intelligence in trials’ emerged as the most frequent new themes suggested. Conclusions This work provides an updated stakeholder-informed agenda for trials methodology research. The top three priorities were designing relevant and impactful trials, ensuring representative participants, and improving recruitment, each appeared in the top 10 for all stakeholder groups. Despite consensus on core priorities, differences between professional and patient-public stakeholders highlight areas for future methodology research and funding.

items.title: Uses of Artificial Intelligence In Geography
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming an important technology in the field of Geography. It helps geographers collect, process, analyze, and interpret large amounts of geographical data quickly and accurately. AI is widely used with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing, satellite images, GPS, and spatial databases. It can help in land-use and land-cover mapping, urban planning, population analysis, disaster management, climate studies, agriculture, and environmental monitoring. AI-based techniques such as machine learning and deep learning can identify patterns and changes in geographical areas that may be difficult to detect through traditional methods. AI also helps in predicting natural hazards such as floods, droughts, landslides, and forest fires. In urban areas, it supports transportation planning, infrastructure development, and smart-city management. In agriculture, AI can assist in crop monitoring, soil analysis, and yield prediction. However, the effective use of AI requires reliable data, skilled users, proper technology, and attention to data privacy and accuracy. Thus, Artificial Intelligence has great potential to improve geographical research, spatial analysis, planning, and sustainable development.

items.title: “Delivering” Culture Change: A Quality Improvement Approach to Nurse-Resident Relations on Labor & Delivery
items.abstract: Background: Strained nurse-resident relations on Labor and Delivery are a widely recognized but inadequately addressed threat linked to adverse outcomes, trainee and nursing distress, hostile clinical learning environments, and patient safety issues. In our institution, a 2024 Program Evaluation Committee meeting SWOT analysis (Strength-Weakness-Opportunity-Threat) identified nurse-resident relations at a busy academic Labor and Delivery unit as an opportunity for improvement within our residency program. Issues included persistent unprofessional behaviors, inadequate and mistrusted reporting mechanisms, and a culture of silence with a fear of retaliation. Objective: To implement and evaluate a quality improvement model for improving nurse-resident relations on Labor & Delivery. Study Design: Using Kotter’s 8-Step Change Model as a framework, a multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative was launched in May 2024 as a joint effort by resident and nursing leadership. Interventions included creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey, recognition of outstanding nurses and residents, monthly interdisciplinary leadership meetings to review concerns, structured social events, clarification and education regarding resident and nursing escalation pathways, and the establishment of a joint Nurse-Resident Workgroup. Results: In two years, a total of 74 nursing and resident-related incidents were submitted and addressed through the creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey. In the first 7 months there were 26 submissions, in the second 7 months there were 41 submissions, and in the final 7 months there were 7 submissions. QR code submissions declined over time, which served as an indicator of culture improvement. A total of 100 kudos were submitted by both nurses and residents recognizing exemplary interprofessional behavior. Monthly nursing-initiated socials were established at the beginning of each resident rotation to intentionally strengthen camaraderie, promote teamwork, and help nurses and incoming interns build familiarity early in the rotation. As a second phase to the improvement efforts, a Nurse-Resident Workgroup was launched in November 2025, completing six structured meetings by June 2026. This workgroup consisted of a core team of 7 front-line nurses and rotating residents with a total of approximately 10 to 12 participants at each session. This in-person discussion was mediated by combined nursing and residency leadership and focused on conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between both nurses and residents without intensive investment outside of this structured time. Participants were anonymously polled at the fourth and fifth workgroup with 12/12 (100%) positive responses at the fourth workgroup and 9/10 (90%) positive responses at the fifth workgroup, with 0 negative responses in both workgroups. In addition, participants suggested 5 topics for future discussion. Conclusions: A structured and leadership-supported quality improvement initiative can meaningfully improve nurse-resident relationships on Labor and Delivery. The Nurse-Resident Workgroup is a replicable intervention that provides a structured venue for conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between nurses and residents. Discussion allows for understanding of diverse perspectives and roles, which ultimately led to system changes across nursing, residency, and faculty teams. This model provides a framework for other residency programs facing similar challenges and can be adapted to different unique Labor & Delivery environments.

items.title: “The pharmacological potential of CRISPR-Cas9: Revolutionizing gene therapy and drug development”
items.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has entered the mainstream of genetic research and therapeutic development, offering a level of programmable and targeted gene editing that has substantially expanded the possibilities of genetic manipulation. This review focuses on the discovery to development of CRISPR-Cas9 and its recent practice in pharmacological and biotechnology field. We discuss further advancements in CRISPR technology such as high-fidelity CRISPR and new systems Cas12 and Cas13 which increases efficiency of editing and opens more opportunities. CRISPR technology has been further advanced when combined with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; guide RNA is now optimized while the off-target effects are predicted. The review also focuses on the new targets for therapy, recent trials, the legal and the social and ethical relevance of the CRISPR approach. With the development of CRISPR-Cas9 promising and revolutionary preliminary achievements in the fields of drug development and disease management and tissue engineering are anticipated. Although, in its application, there are questions that have been raised concerning side effects, carriers, and ethics, it is important to take advantage of it in the right manner. As seen in this review, CRISPR-Cas9 plays the crucial part of the development of biomedical studies and therapeutic paradigms.

items.title: 29. Introducing Data Science Concepts to Animal Science Graduate Students Through Application-based Learning.
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science into biological research has created a growing need for computational literacy among graduate students in life science disciplines. However, many students’ entering biology-related graduate programs have limited formal training in programming, statistics, or machine learning, creating a significant barrier to engaging with modern data-driven research. The objective of this study was to evaluate baseline perceptions of AI and data science among animal science students prior to participating in a course introducing these concepts through application-based learning. A pre-course perception survey was administered to students enrolled in an introductory AI and data science course in animal science (n = 10). Survey questions used a 5-point Likert scale to assess prior programming experience, familiarity with AI concepts, attitudes toward AI applications in animal science and motivation to learn these skills. Students reported limited prior experience with programming languages (mean = 2.9 ± 1.45) and moderate use of AI tools in daily life (mean = 2.98 ± 1.32). Despite limited technical exposure, students indicated moderate understanding of basic AI and data science concepts (mean = 3.6 ± 0.70 and 3.6 ± 0.52, respectively). Participants expressed strong agreement that AI and data science can be effectively applied in animal science (mean = 3.9 ± 0.57) and that learning these skills would benefit their academic or professional development (mean = 4.0 ± 0.67). Students also expressed moderate motivation to learn AI applications in livestock systems (mean = 3.5 ± 1.08). While this project provides the current perceptions of students and their skill levels in AI and data science, a follow-up post survey to assess the effects of such a course, and combining it with a Mann-Whiteney U test will further inform the required pedagogical shifts. These preliminary findings highlight the value of interdisciplinary teaching approaches that integrate biological applications with computational methods (such as an AI in animal science course) and may inform curriculum design for graduate programs seeking to prepare life science students for increasingly data-intensive research environments.

items.title: 367. Multi-modal Machine Learning for the Early Detection of Subclinical Ketosis in Dairy Cattle.
items.abstract: Abstract Subclinical ketosis (SCK) is a prevalent metabolic disorder in transition dairy cows causing significant economic and welfare impacts, yet early detection remains challenging due to absent clinical signs and disease complexity. Two complementary projects developed multi-modal machine learning systems for prepartum prediction of postpartum SCK risk. The first integrated depth image-derived body shape features (extracted via CNN, anatomical keypoint sampling, and CNN-RNN), wearable sensor behavioral data, cow history, and text embeddings from farm management notes using generic and fine-tuned LLMs; Random Forest models combining image and tabular data achieved F₁ = 0.706, with fine-tuned LLM text embeddings further improving sensor-based models (F₁ 0.681 vs. 0.655). The second project added genomic data (78,964 SNPs reduced to 128 dimensions via UMAP) and introduced a cloud-based modular pipeline for automated image processing and data integration; among three fusion strategies tested, late fusion achieved the highest performance (F₁ up to 0.750) for binary SCK classification. Together, these projects show that integrating phenomic and genomic data through modern machine learning and fusion techniques substantially improves early SCK detection, supporting preventive health management in dairy farms.
